source.title: A Combinatorial Theory of Dropout: Subnetworks, Graph Geometry, and Generalization

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendices; no apparent truncation.
record.tranche_reason: It tests dropout’s relation to generalization through subnetwork contribution scores, entropy, connectivity, and width sweeps, but its own arguments and results have major assumptions and inconsistencies that require narrowing its claims. It does not test most of the listed versions directly.
record.gate_note: Rows cover the paper's reported experiments on dropout subnetworks, generalization-gap proxies, entropy, and width. The study does not compare random-label memorization with natural-label generalization, optimizer or batch-size choices, or fully connected versus convolutional networks. The dropout-related results bear on V6 only where they directly measure dropout's effect on held-out error; these experiments generally measure subnetwork scores or other properties instead.
record.test_reason: The study measures dropout-subnetwork output agreement, train–test loss differences, graph connectivity, entropy, and bound comparisons. It does not compare held-out error with versus without dropout, test error beyond interpolation, or magnitude-aware weight sharpness. Its theoretical arguments concern these different outcomes and do not establish or contest any listed version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate but understates the authors' assertions. They claim to prove smooth, densely connected, low-resistance clusters of generalizing subnetworks, PAC-Bayes guarantees, and exponential growth with width, and claim that experiments validate every theoretical result. These assertions concern their contribution-score framework rather than a measured reduction in held-out error from adding dropout.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies dropout-trained subnetworks and contribution scores rather than the claim versions' interventions or measures. Its experiments use SGD, fixed retain probability p = 0.8, no weight decay, short fixed epoch counts, and several architectures/datasets.
record.method_sensitivity: Architecture and dataset appear in the reported output-approximation, entropy, and PAC-Bayes results. Width and depth change the figure-only fraction of sampled subnetworks passing the contribution-score threshold. Linear experiments omit ReLU; ResNet-18 is omitted from those tests.

fits_no_version.finding: Dropout-averaged outputs approximately match scaled linear-model outputs; full-model and ensemble classifications agree on 94.78–99.95% of examples.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Linear dropout models can approximate subnetwork ensembles in output or prediction agreement.

fits_no_version.finding: The paper reports sampled subnetworks passing its train–test loss-gap threshold and zero sampled-graph Dirichlet energy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Dropout-trained subnetworks have small and locally stable train–test loss differences in the tested sampling procedures.

fits_no_version.finding: Entropy of averaged predictions is slightly higher for incorrectly classified examples in all four configurations.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Dropout-ensemble predictive entropy is associated with classification correctness.

fits_no_version.finding: Reported average subnetwork test losses fall below the reported PAC-Bayes bounds.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The paper's computed bounds exceed its measured average subnetwork test losses.

fits_no_version.finding: Reported correlations between graph resistance and absolute contribution-score differences range from 0.0366 to 0.0789.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Graph resistance has a weak positive association with differences in subnetwork train–test loss gaps in these experiments.

fits_no_version.finding: The sampled fraction below the contribution-score threshold increases with width and depth, reportedly reaching 100%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Wider and deeper dropout-trained MNIST MLPs yield more sampled subnetworks passing a train–test loss-gap threshold.

record.problems: The experiments use only MNIST and CIFAR-10, four model setups, short training schedules, fixed dropout and SGD settings, and no weight decay; the paper itself says larger-scale settings and highly nonlinear regimes remain to be explored. Most generalization results are described as aggregate prose or figure-only. The score C(f) is defined using expected test loss minus empirical training loss, while the experimental section writes it as Ltest(f) − Ltrain(f); no test-error comparisons with and without dropout are reported. The reported CI/standard-deviation values are inconsistent in places (for example, Table 2 gives a CNN + MNIST incorrect entropy CI95 of ±0.0886 alongside ±0.0357). The appendix's theoretical derivations assume key conclusions such as low score variation or dense coverage rather than establishing them from the stated premises.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted due to the 60-row cap. Figure-only numeric values were not reconstructed; the width sweep is represented by R27 with the paper's textual description and figure locator.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting, natural-label held-out accuracy, and chance-level held-out accuracy under random labels.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected classification error and the role of learned or imposed local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning and recovery interventions.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Held-out error with versus without dropout, small-data effects, excessive dropout, and joint removal of dropout and weight decay with augmentation.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, its ranking of generalization gaps, and comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: Correct the record's V6 status from tested_not_extracted to not_tested. Methodological weaknesses in this paper do not themselves challenge any claim version. All judgments use only the supplied text.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting versus natural-label generalization and held-out accuracy.
Width sweep does not test test error beyond the interpolation threshold; it counts sampled subnetworks passing a contribution-score threshold.
No fully connected versus convolutional comparison of test error.

The paper applies dropout but does not compare test error with and without dropout, on small training sets, or against dropout plus weight-decay removal. Its measured outcomes are dropout subnetwork properties, not the version's test-error effect.
No magnitude-aware sharpness measurement or comparison with norm- and margin-based measures.
No removal of memorized training examples.
